channel.title: The San Francisco Standard - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: Risking fury from parents, SF teachers vote to approve first school strike since ’79
item.description: Roughly 6,000 educators may soon hit the picket lines, prompting a scramble for child care.

item.title: The Giants’ elder statesman, Dusty Baker, hopes Tony Vitello will get ‘extended chance’
item.description: In a wide-ranging discussion at the Giants’ FanFest stop in West Sacramento, the team’s former manager talked about the roster, free-agents fits, and more.

item.title: How three-time batting champion Luis Arráez will fit with the Giants
item.description: Buster Posey turned to the free agent market to add a left-handed hitting second baseman.

item.title: Booze shots are out. Cheekies are in
item.description: No one can agree on how the ritual started, but downing a cheeky is now the currency of cool in SF bars.

item.title: Luis Arráez is exactly the type of player the Giants have been missing
item.description: Buster Posey’s bet on MLB’s contact king will reshape a lineup that should be far more aesthetically pleasing than last year’s.

item.title: Kawakami: Deciphering the Giants’ plan — all about a pending Dodgers reckoning?
item.description: When MLB’s new labor deal arrives, maybe we’ll see the true impact of this zen offseason for Buster Posey and San Francisco’s front office.

item.title: How the Outer Sunset’s real estate market is surfing the white-collar wave
item.description: Seven-figure listings, new restaurants, and a changing guard signal a beachfront shift at the city’s westside.

item.title: All the ways San Franciscans are finding joy amidst the chaos
item.description: Answers from our recent live podcast taping ranged from “learn piano” and “make pizza” to “do more drugs” and “quit my job.”

item.title: A new pro volleyball team wants in on San Francisco’s women’s sports boom
item.description: League One Volleyball is expanding to the Bay Area, and team president Stephanie Martin sees an opportunity to thrive.

item.title: Raheem Morris could be the 49ers’ long-term solution as defensive coordinator
item.description: After multiple failed stints as a head coach, Morris is reuniting with Kyle Shanahan in San Francisco.
